Hi Alice / Orbis security team — Neha from Redwood Security here. I wanted to provide the technical details you'll need for your RFP considerations and the upcoming mapping session. Key points below; happy to expand on any bullet during the workshop.

SAML / OIDC (SSO)
- SAML: We support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. Signed assertions required; we recommend assertion signing + response signing for high-assurance integrations.
- NameID formats: persistent, emailAddress, and transient supported.
- Assertion attributes: full attribute whitelist configurable per SP (e.g., email, displayName, groups, employeeNumber, manager).
- Encryption: optional assertion encryption (RSA-OAEP / AES-GCM).
- Audience & Recipient checks enforced; assertion lifetime default 5 minutes (configurable).
- OIDC: Full OIDC (Authorization Code + PKCE) for browser/native apps. Standard endpoints: /oauth2/authorize, /oauth2/token, /oauth2/introspect, /oauth2/revoke. Access token TTL default 1h, refresh token TTL 30d (refresh rotation optional).
- Introspection and revocation: introspection endpoint supports token metadata and active flag; revocation endpoint supports immediate invalidation.

SCIM (user and group provisioning)
- SCIM protocol: SCIM 2.0 (RFC7644) implemented. Endpoints: /scim/v2/Users and /scim/v2/Groups.
- Delta sync: We support incremental synchronization using the "startIndex/totalResults" and delta tokens ({lastModified} based). Delete handling: we return 404 for missing resources unless the client requests list with excluded attributes; we also emit "status": "deleted" in change events when using event-based sync.
- Bulk operations: supported for initial bulk push (POST /Bulk) up to 500 operations per request; we advise batching to avoid rate limits.
- Group -> role mapping: recommended pattern is group.externalId -> role.externalId mapping. We include group membership changes within 5–15s in normal operation; worst-case eventual consistency up to 60s under high load.
- Custom attributes & schema extension: supports enterprise extension urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User (employeeNumber, costCenter).
- SCIM rate limits: default 120 req/min per tenant; can be increased for Dedicated customers via contract.
- Error semantics: idempotent PUT/PATCH with standard HTTP status codes; 429 with Retry-After when throttled.

RBAC & Admin Controls
- Built-in roles: Owner (full control), Admin (manage resources), Operator (deploy/run), Read-Only Auditor (view-only), Support (limited debug access).
- Custom roles: Customers can create granular roles with allow/deny policies at the resource/action level (e.g., models:invoke, infra:scale).
- Delegated admin: We support provisioning admin flag via SCIM (User.active + enterprise extension roles attribute) and scoped admin tokens bound to a role and a project/tenant. Delegated admin actions are recorded with an immutable audit trail.
- Separation of duties: RBAC rules can be layered with approval workflows for sensitive operations (e.g., enabling billing exports or changing encryption keys).

Audit, Logging & Evidence
- Admin activity audit logs: immutable append-only audit with actor, action, timestamp, resource, and before/after snapshots. Default retention 180 days; enterprise plans configurable to 7+ years.
- Access logs: token introspection events, SSO assertions (metadata only), and SCIM provisioning deltas are recorded. Sample log extract attached (audit_sample.log).

Implementation notes & test artifacts
- We provide a SAML metadata template (saml_config_template.xml) and a sample SCIM mapping CSV (scim_mapping_example.csv) to accelerate onboarding.
- Staging: we can provide a temporary staging tenant (URL + scoped API key) for the workshop; we will exchange credentials over a secure channel once NDA is in place. See staging_tenant_access.txt for placeholder details.

If helpful, we can pre-run a SCIM dry-run against a subset of users you provide (non-production) and report the delta / mapping changes.

Thanks Neha — a couple of quick clarifications before the workshop:

1) Delta tokens & deletes: can you confirm the delta token format (timestamp vs opaque token) and whether your SCIM implementation can emit tombstone entries for deleted users so downstream systems can reconcile?

2) Group-role mapping: you mentioned 5–15s propagation for membership changes. For our compliance posture we need role revocation to be reflected in < 60s for production accounts. Is that SLA possible in Dedicated or Private deployments?

3) Delegated admin: we need separation of duties between tenant admin (can onboard users) and security admin (can change RBAC policies). Can delegated admins be limited to onboarding only (no RBAC edits) and will those actions be separately logged?

We prefer to run the workshop the week after next if you can provide more detailed answers to the above so we can prepare internal test data.

Regards,

OrbisBank Security Team
From: chloe.martin@redwood.com

Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, security@orbisbank.com

Subject: Re: Request: IAM capabilities & SCIM mapping for Redwood evaluation

Hi Alice / Security team — quick answers and next steps, and thanks for the thoughtful questions.

1) Delta tokens & tombstones: our delta token is an opaque token tied to a last-synced timestamp on our side; for event-based integrations we can include tombstone entries (status: "deleted") in the change array. We'll include a short sample in the workshop packet.

2) Propagation SLA: for Hosted customers we guarantee typical propagation under 60s; for Dedicated/Private we can include a strict <60s SLA as part of the capacity commitment and autoscaling configuration (this is commonly added to the contract). We will flag this for legal / commercial.

3) Delegated admin separation: yes — delegated admins can be scoped to only onboarding actions (create/update users) and cannot change RBAC policies unless explicitly granted. All delegated admin actions are recorded in the audit trail and surfaced in the Console as distinct actor types.

Workshop: Wed 6 Oct 09:00–10:00 CET or Thu 7 Oct 15:00–16:00 CET — please pick one. Agenda will include the short mapping dry-run (we'll provision a synthetic user set), live SCIM push, and RBAC scenarios.
